STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a flat, pale square-ish plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no curved inner wall. This is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. The plate here looks medium-large, roughly a standard dinner size.
b) Reference: almonds are 2.3 cm long. Across the plate's long diagonal-ish width, the plate spans roughly 11-12 almond lengths along its visible width (about 26-28 cm of almonds laid end to end is consistent with the plate width). Counting across the plate from left edge to right edge gives about 11-12 almonds, so width ≈ 11.5 × 2.3 ≈ 26 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Almonds (countable). Visible count: roughly 60 whole almonds plus a few halves/broken ones, about 65 pieces visible. The pile is about 2 deep in the centre, so add hidden ones: the mound is mostly one layer with some stacking, so take about 70 almonds total at 1.2 g each = 84 g.
- Check via footprint: the almond pile covers about 35% of the plate area. Plate area = 625 cm² (square 25 cm), footprint ≈ 0.35 × 625 ≈ 219 cm². Average thickness ≈ 1.2 cm (one almond thick, with some stacking at the centre). Volume ≈ 263 ml, almond bulk density for whole nuts is about 0.45 g/ml, giving ≈ 118 g. Count-based (84 g) and volume-based (118 g) disagree; the almonds are shell-less kernels with air gaps, so I'll weight toward the count: about 95 g.

Hidden food: no base layer beneath; the plate is bare underneath the almonds. A small yellow fleck on the plate is negligible.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: only the almond stack; no added base layer.

STEP 5 - Energy: raw almonds ≈ 579 kcal per 100 g.

Total: about 95 g of almonds.
